correctness.rationale: For any fixed base sequence, each of the m residue chains can be solved in both directions from an arbitrary initial symbol. Hence every prefix through length m occurs and the unrestricted palindrome count applies there. For n>m the difference block of a reflected word is the negative of the reflected difference block: v_(n-m-1-i)=-v_i for a palindrome. Both signs lie in B, hence every v_i is zero. Conversely any finite m-periodic palindrome extends using an occurrence of 0^(n-m) and its first m letters as the lift seed. Thus all such words occur exactly through length m+L. For n>m every residue occurs and the congruence 2r=n-1 mod m gives the fixed points of the reflection on residues; fixed points and transposed pairs account for all (m+f_m(n-1))/2 choices of independent symbols. The parity laws and the count after subtracting the q constant words at m+1 follow. The Fibonacci substitution has 00 but no 000 (substituted isolated 1's can contribute at most one extra 0 to a run), so L=2. The lag m in the stated code is block length m+1 in Kang–Jäger, whose theorem covers all these Fibonacci lifts.
residual_risks: The zero-run criterion does not apply to alphabets admitting a nonzero opposite pair, including the usual binary modulus-two difference lift. Recorded finite checks do not prove the full profile.
